definition: Example-based machine translation (EBMT) is a method of machine translation often characterized by its use of a bilingual corpus with parallel texts as its main knowledge base at run-time.
details: It is essentially a translation by analogy and can be viewed as an implementation of a case-based reasoning approach to machine learning.

explainer.lead: Example-based machine translation (EBMT) translates new text by analogy with examples in a bilingual corpus of parallel texts. It shows how existing translations can serve directly as a system’s main knowledge base at run time.

tiers.eli5: Imagine learning to translate by looking at pairs of sentences in two languages and using similar pairs to work out a new one. EBMT does something like this: it keeps those examples handy while translating and reasons by analogy.
tiers.practitioner: In an EBMT system, the bilingual parallel-text corpus is the main knowledge base used at run time. The engineering task is to support translation by analogy from those examples, following a case-based reasoning approach to machine learning.
tiers.paperLevel: EBMT can be summarized as: (source text, bilingual parallel-text corpus at run time) -> translation by analogy. It is characterized by using that corpus as its main run-time knowledge base and can be viewed as case-based reasoning applied to machine learning.

explainer.example: Suppose the corpus pairs “the cat runs” with “le chat court” and “the dog sleeps” with “le chien dort.” By analogy across the two pairs, EBMT could translate “the dog runs” as “le chien court.”

usedIn.name: Case-based reasoning
usedIn.detail: EBMT can be viewed as an implementation of this machine-learning approach.

explainer.intuition: Instead of treating translation as only a matter of isolated words, EBMT uses previously paired texts as examples. A new translation is produced by analogy with those examples.
howItWorks: Start with a bilingual corpus containing parallel texts.
Keep that corpus available as the main knowledge base at run time.
Compare the new source text with the available translation examples.
Produce the target translation by analogy with those examples.
explainer.whyItMatters: EBMT makes translated examples themselves the central run-time resource. It also connects machine translation to the broader idea of case-based reasoning.
misconceptions: EBMT is not simply word-for-word substitution: its central idea is translation by analogy using parallel texts.
The bilingual corpus is not merely background material; it is characteristically the main knowledge base at run time.
